title: deployment
description: One release of code to a running environment during the audit period — a GitHub Deployment, a GitLab deployment to an environment. Paired with pull_request it answers the question a configuration snapshot cannot: did the code now running in production come through the reviewed path? Plugins emit one record per deployment whose creation timestamp falls inside the collection window, including failed ones — a failed production deployment is still a change event an auditor may ask about. Environment naming is vendor- and customer-specific (`production`, `prod`, `live`), so the plugin normalizes the classification into is_production rather than leaving policies to pattern-match strings. status is likewise normalized to a small closed vocabulary because GitHub reports deployment state through a separate statuses sub-resource while GitLab carries it on the deployment itself.

repository.description: Repository the deployment came from, in the same form git_repository uses for `name` (typically `org/repo`).

deployment_id.description: Vendor-native deployment identifier, as a string so numeric and opaque IDs share one shape.

environment.description: Environment name exactly as the vendor reports it, preserved verbatim for the audit trail. Do not branch policies on this — use is_production, which is normalized.

is_production.description: True when this deployment targeted production. Derived by the plugin from whatever signal the vendor offers — GitHub's production_environment flag or an environment name of production/prod/live; GitLab's environment tier of `production`. Normalizing here keeps the customer's local naming conventions out of the policy set.

deployed_by.description: Username that triggered the deployment. Empty string when the vendor attributes it to no user (a deleted account, or a pipeline running under a project token).

commit_sha.description: Commit SHA that was deployed. Joins to pull_request.merge_commit_sha to trace a running release back to the change that was reviewed. Empty string when the vendor reports none, which fails the trace closed.

status.description: Normalized terminal state. `success` — the deployment reported success. `failure` — it errored, failed, or was cancelled. `pending` — created, queued, or still running. `unknown` — the vendor reported no state at all (a GitHub deployment with no status entries), which is distinct from pending and must not be read as either success or failure.
